after.worked_solution:
To find the domain of $f$, we need the intersection of the domains of the individual components.

- The domain of the 1st component $t$ is $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

- The domain of the 2nd component $\operatorname{csc}⁡(2t)$ is $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ),$ except for the values of $t$ for which

$$
2t=\pi n\,⟹\,t=\frac{\pi n}{2},
$$

where $n$ is an integer.

- The domain of the 3rd component $1+{t}^{2}$ is $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

Therefore, the domain of the vector-valued function $f(t)$ is 

$$
t\in (-\infty ,\infty ),\,t\ne \frac{\pi n}{2},
$$

where $n$ is an integer.

Find the domain of the vector-valued function f(s)=⟨s,ln⁡(2−s),3⟩.

b

To find the domain of f, we need the intersection of the domains of the individual components.

  • The domain of the 1st component s is s∈[0,∞).

  • The domain of the 2nd component ln⁡(2−s) is s∈(−∞,2).

  • The domain of the 3rd component 3 is s∈(−∞,∞).

The intersection is illustrated in the diagram below.

Therefore, the domain of the vector-valued function f(s) is s∈[0,2).
